title: Throwing a matched set of cereal bowls
subtitle: Six matching wide-mouth bowls thrown to consistent measurements
excerpt: Throwing a matched set of six cereal bowls teaches the production-pottery skill of repeating dimensions across multiple pieces. The goal is bowls within 5 mm of each other in height and rim diameter. This tutorial covers using a throwing gauge and calipers to hold dimensions across the set.
sourceNotes: Technique synthesised from standard production throwing references and practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: A fixed reference point set at the rim height of the first bowl; used to check that subsequent bowls are the same height
A narrow raised ring trimmed at the base of a wheel-thrown piece to give a finished base and raise the piece slightly

content.text: Matching a set comes down to measuring before removing each piece from the wheel. Use a

made from a stick of wood fixed to the wheel splash pan: set its tip to the rim height of the first finished bowl and use it to check all subsequent pieces. Set the calipers to the rim diameter of the first bowl and check each piece before wiring off.

materials.name: Smooth stoneware clay, 350 g per bowl

content.text: Centre 350 g. Open to a floor about 8 mm thick. Pull the wall upward and outward to a wide curved bowl form: a height of 8 cm and rim diameter of 16 cm. Leave the wall at 5 to 6 mm thick.
Finish the rim with two wet fingers. Set the throwing gauge to the rim height and the calipers to the rim diameter. Record these measurements. Wire off and set aside.
Weigh each subsequent piece of clay to 350 g before centering. Throw each bowl to the gauge height and caliper diameter. Check both before wiring off.
Make small corrections by pulling the rim in or out slightly at the finishing step. A rim 3 mm off diameter is easier to correct now than to notice after bisque firing.
Wire each bowl off the wheel and place on a board. Space evenly for uniform drying.
When leather-hard, invert each bowl on the wheel and trim a

about 12 mm wide and 6 mm tall. Trim all six foot rings to the same diameter by measuring from the caliper set before trimming the first. A uniform foot ring makes the set look professionally matched when stacked.

items.problem: Bowls are not staying at the gauge height and keep coming out shorter
items.cause: The clay is collapsing slightly before wiring off, losing height; or the weighed clay amount is inconsistent
items.fix: Weigh clay more precisely. Check that the gauge is set to the final finished bowl rim, not to a point above it. Accept that a 3 to 5 mm variation in height is normal for hand-thrown sets

items.problem: Set looks mismatched even though the measurements are right
items.cause: The wall curvature profile varies between pieces even when height and rim diameter match
items.fix: Throw all pieces on the same day so hand position and rhythm are consistent. After trimming, line all six up and compare the wall curve profiles visually; minor differences in curve register more strongly than small size differences
